entities.summary: The Khujandi family was a Shafi'i family of religious scholars based in the city of Isfahan in central Iran, who played a leading role in Isfahani politics during the Seljuk era and up until the Mongol invasion. Their name refers to their hometown of Khujand in Transoxiana, which was then under Qarakhanid rule. The founder of the family was Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Thabit al-Khujandi, who was appointed the head of a Shafi'i school in Isfahan by the Persian vizier of the Seljuks, Nizam al-Mulk. After Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Thabit al-Khujandi, Abu Mahmud Hamid ibn al-Khidr al-Khujandi became the identity of khujandi family.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Khujandi family played a significant role in Isfahan politics during the Seljuk era, with their Shafi'i school influencing Islamic scholarship and governance. Their legacy continued to shape regional intellectual and cultural developments after the Mongol invasion.
